methods.name: add_alternative

methods.name: first

methods.name: into_alternatives
methods.summary: Returns all alternatives as a vector of `LexRequirement` objects and a boolean value indicating softness/hardness of the requirements.

methods.name: into_single

items.name: LexOrdering
items.summary: This object represents a lexicographical ordering and contains a vector of `PhysicalSortExpr` objects.

methods.name: capacity
methods.summary: Returns the number of elements that can be stored in the `LexOrdering` without reallocating.

methods.name: extend
methods.signature: fn extend(&mut self, sort_exprs: impl IntoIterator<Item = PhysicalSortExpr>)
methods.summary: Add all elements from `iter` to the `LexOrdering`.

methods.name: first
methods.summary: Returns the leading `PhysicalSortExpr` of the `LexOrdering`. Note that this function does not return an `Option`, as a `LexOrdering` is always non-degenerate (i.e. it contains at least one element).

methods.name: get_sort_options
methods.summary: Returns the sort options for the given expression if one is defined in this `LexOrdering`.

methods.name: is_reverse
methods.summary: Check if reversing this ordering would satisfy another ordering requirement.

methods.name: new
methods.signature: fn new(exprs: impl IntoIterator<Item = PhysicalSortExpr>) -> Option<Self>
methods.summary: Creates a new [`LexOrdering`] from the given vector of sort expressions. If the vector is empty, returns `None`.

methods.name: push
methods.summary: Appends an element to the back of the `LexOrdering`.

methods.name: truncate
methods.signature: fn truncate(&mut self, len: usize) -> bool
methods.summary: Truncates the `LexOrdering`, keeping only the first `len` elements. Returns `true` if truncation made a change, `false` otherwise. Negative cases happen in two scenarios: (1) When `len` is greater than or equal to the number of expressions…

items.name: LexRequirement
items.summary: This object represents a lexicographical ordering requirement and contains a vector of `PhysicalSortRequirement` objects.

methods.name: first
methods.summary: Returns the leading `PhysicalSortRequirement` of the `LexRequirement`. Note that this function does not return an `Option`, as a `LexRequirement` is always non-degenerate (i.e. it contains at least one element).

methods.name: new
methods.signature: fn new(reqs: impl IntoIterator<Item = PhysicalSortRequirement>) -> Option<Self>
methods.summary: Creates a new [`LexRequirement`] from the given vector of sort expressions. If the vector is empty, returns `None`.

items.name: PhysicalSortExpr
items.summary: Represents Sort operation for a column in a RecordBatch

methods.name: asc
methods.summary: Set the sort sort options to ASC

methods.name: desc
methods.summary: Set the sort sort options to DESC

methods.name: evaluate_to_sort_column
methods.summary: Evaluates the sort expression into a `SortColumn` that can be passed into the arrow sort kernel.

methods.name: fmt_sql
methods.summary: Like [`PhysicalExpr::fmt_sql`] prints a [`PhysicalSortExpr`] in a SQL-like format.

methods.name: from
methods.summary: The default sort options `ASC, NULLS LAST` when the requirement does not specify sort options. This default is consistent with PostgreSQL.

methods.name: new
methods.signature: fn new(expr: Arc<dyn PhysicalExpr>, options: SortOptions) -> Self
methods.summary: Create a new PhysicalSortExpr

methods.name: new_default
methods.summary: Create a new PhysicalSortExpr with default [`SortOptions`]

methods.name: nulls_first
methods.summary: Set the sort sort options to NULLS FIRST

methods.name: nulls_last
methods.summary: Set the sort sort options to NULLS LAST

methods.name: reverse
methods.summary: Reverses the sort expression. For instance, `[a ASC NULLS LAST]` turns into `[a DESC NULLS FIRST]`. Such reversals are useful in planning, e.g. when constructing equivalent window expressions.

methods.name: satisfy
methods.summary: Checks whether this sort expression satisfies the given `requirement`. If sort options are unspecified in `requirement`, only expressions are compared for inequality. See [`options_compatible`] for details on how sort options compare with…

methods.name: satisfy_expr
methods.summary: Checks whether this sort expression satisfies the given `sort_expr`. See [`options_compatible`] for details on how sort options compare with one another.

methods.name: try_from_proto
methods.summary: Reconstruct a [`PhysicalSortExpr`] from its protobuf representation.

methods.name: try_to_proto
methods.summary: Serialize this sort expression, encoding its child expression through `ctx`.
